subject.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps

question: Should onboarding transmit installed macOS application names to the configured model and ClawHub by default after disclosure, or require explicit consent before the first external lookup?
rationale: The implementation intentionally chooses default-on external inventory matching, while repository policy treats privacy boundaries, new defaults, configuration, setup behavior, and fallbacks as maintainer-owned product decisions.

options.title: Require consent first
options.body: Prompt before scanning or transmitting application names, while keeping node-host inventory sharing separately default-off and explicit.

options.title: Sponsor default-on disclosure
options.body: Explicitly accept the default-on privacy model, document the boundary, and still require the path-removal, setup-integration, upgrade, and live-proof fixes before merge.

options.title: Keep discovery local by default
options.body: Use local official-catalog matching first and make model or ClawHub enrichment an explicit opt-in step.

recommendation.title: Require consent first
recommendation.body: Prompt before scanning or transmitting application names, while keeping node-host inventory sharing separately default-off and explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch, self-assignment, and onboarding redesign history place the product and privacy direction with this feature owner.
